title: Late fees + refunded section: two branches that must not couple
description: Type K (local failure isolation). Two genuinely independent features (late fee in invoice.py; refunded section in reports.py) share only the invoice record format in store.py. The plan must keep the branches uncoupled — no edge between them — so a local failure in one branch (e.g. the fee math breaks) does not re-plan the other, and each branch's task must be locally recoverable (checkpoint handoff required). Anti-plans: a 'billing improvements' mega-task coupling both branches, a cross-branch edge (fake dependency), or restructuring the shared record format as part of one branch.

anchors.description: shared invoice record format (frozen contract both branches read/write)

must_freeze.note: the invoice record format in the store is the shared frozen contract; neither branch may restructure it (additive optional fields only)

must_have_edges.note: the late-fee branch extends the shared record format additively
the report branch reads shared records (status field)

must_not_have_edges.reason: independent branches sharing only the store record format; no data, contract, or ownership flow between the late-fee and refunded-section work — a failure in one must not re-plan the other

parallelizable_groups.note: the two branches are disjoint closures and run in parallel

expected.notes: Type K probe: local recoverability + branch isolation. Both branch tasks must declare checkpoint handoff (recoverable_tasks). A plan that serializes or cross-couples the branches (edge A1<->A2, or one task owning both files — cap is 1) fails the isolation constraints. Range [3, 6]: two branch tasks + shared-contract/e2e task(s).
